doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Later years with Goodman and the final break in Australia
summary: Playing with Goodman at the Rainbow Grill while on the Tonight Show, then leaving after the 'ray' on an Australian tour.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: But then, years later, you know I was getting successful then, I was in the NBC band with Doc Severinsen and then, as soon as I finished “The Tonight Show” at seven I’d run upstairs and play with Benny Goodman at the Rainbow Grill, it was all in the same building. I was working like night and day. And I got very close to Benny then, and that was an equal mistake. He would call me up and say, “well what do you think of so-and- so, what do you think of so-and-so,” before they hired them. And then the ax fell, as it does with everybody. I think it’s 1973 or something. I was still on staff at NBC doing “The Tonight Show” every day, and Benny called and said, “hey look, Pops, we’re going down to Australia. It’s a great trip, and you really ought to come.” I said, “well I’ll try and get out of NBC.” And so I did and I got my wife’s mother and father to come in from England to look after the kids, and we made all this—and we went to Australia. And there we played the first rehearsal and Benny started looking at me funny. He’s looking over the clarinet at me. I said what’s going on? And that’s “the ray.” And everybody got it, it doesn’t matter who you were. Everybody got it. And I looked at him, and we exchanged a few choice words, and I finished out the tune and never saw him again. But it still doesn’t detract, he was the greatest jazz clarinet player. I never understood him as a man but he sure could play.
